name: Jump Rope
summary: A continuous cardiovascular and plyometric exercise where you rhythmically jump over a revolving rope.

setup: Adjust the jump rope length so the handles reach approximately armpit or mid-chest height when standing on the middle of the cord.
Stand tall with feet close together, knees softly unlocked, and elbows tucked close to your ribcage with hands slightly forward.
steps: Rotate your wrists to swing the rope over your head and toward your feet.
As the rope approaches the floor, spring off the balls of your feet just high enough (about one to two inches) to clear the rope.
Land softly on the balls of your feet with knees slightly bent to absorb impact, immediately rebounding into the next jump.
Maintain a steady, rhythmic cadence driven primarily by wrist rotation rather than whole-arm swinging.
instructions.breathing: Breathe rhythmically and consistently through the nose and mouth in sync with your jumping cadence.
cues: Turn with the wrists, not the elbows
Stay light on the balls of your feet
Jump only high enough to clear the cable
Keep elbows glued near your ribs

common_faults.fault: Swinging the rope using large shoulder or arm circles instead of wrist rotation.
common_faults.correction: Tuck elbows into your sides and use small circular flicks of the wrists to propel the rope.

common_faults.fault: Jumping too high or kicking heels backward (donkey-kicking).
common_faults.correction: Keep your jumps low and compact, flexing only slightly at the knees and ankles to clear the floor by an inch or two.

common_faults.fault: Landing flat-footed or on your heels.
common_faults.correction: Stay springy and upright, absorbing impact exclusively through the balls of the feet and calves.

precautions: Perform on a forgiving surface like rubber flooring, a wooden floor, or a mat rather than bare concrete to reduce lower-leg impact stress.
Ensure clear overhead and surrounding space to prevent the rope from catching on obstacles.
